questions.q: In Jinja2 syntax, what does {{ domain }} do inside a template?
options: Starts a loop over a list called domain
Inserts the value of the domain variable into the rendered output
Comments out the rest of the line
Defines a new variable named domain
questions.explain: Double curly braces {{ }} are Jinja2's syntax for inserting a value. {% %} tags, by contrast, hold logic like loops and conditionals.

options: Nothing; it writes directly to a file with no return value
A Jinja2 Environment object
The fully rendered template as a string, with placeholders replaced
A dict of the values that were passed in
questions.explain: render() fills in the template with the given values and returns the finished text as a Python string, which you can then print or write to a file.

questions.q: Northbridge's backend pool grows from 3 servers to 4. Using the {% for server in backend_servers %} loop pattern, what has to change?
options: The Jinja2 template file needs a new hardcoded server block added
Nothing changes; the template auto-detects new servers on disk
Only the Python list of backend_servers needs a new entry; the template itself is untouched
The template must be rewritten entirely in a different templating language
questions.explain: A {% for %} loop renders one block per item in whatever list is passed in, so adding a server means adding one entry to the Python list, not editing the template.

questions.q: What is the main practical benefit of generating dev/staging/production configs from one Jinja2 template instead of maintaining three separate files by hand?
options: It makes the files render faster in a browser
It removes the risk of one environment's config silently drifting from another because a change wasn't copied by hand
It automatically encrypts the generated config files
It eliminates the need for any environment variables at all
questions.explain: One template plus per-environment data generates every config correctly and consistently, eliminating the drift risk that comes from manually keeping near-identical files in sync.

questions.q: Which Jinja2 objects are used to locate and load a template file from a directory?
options: json.load and json.loads
yaml.safe_load
Environment and FileSystemLoader
os.environ
questions.explain: Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader("templates")) sets up Jinja2 to find templates in a given directory, and env.get_template(name) loads a specific one.
